note: INS, GNSS, and terrain nav are the three primary autonomous navigation methods, often fused together
INS timing and atomic clocks share error modeling and Allan deviation characterization
GNSS receivers discipline local clocks; atomic clocks provide holdover during GNSS denial
Radar and sonar share waveform design, matched filtering, CFAR detection, and tracking algorithms
Radar and EO sensors are complementary sensing modalities for surveillance and targeting
Sonar bathymetry feeds underwater terrain-referenced navigation
Magnetic anomaly maps enable magnetic-referenced navigation similar to terrain matching
Precision measurement and time-frequency metrology share uncertainty analysis and SPC methods
EO/IR sensors (lidar) provide terrain measurement for terrain-referenced navigation
INS provides attitude and motion compensation for radar antenna stabilization and SAR
GNSS is the primary source of precise time; time-frequency metrology validates GNSS timing
Magnetic and acoustic sensors are the primary passive detection modalities for underwater targets
Clock characterization is a precision measurement process using GUM uncertainty methods
Radar and GNSS share RF front-end design, signal processing, and Doppler estimation techniques
Magnetometer heading aids INS alignment; INS provides platform compensation data for magnetic surveys
